title: Ancient DNA on the map: 16,496 ancient genomes, placed where and when they lived
excerpt: I mapped every ancient human genome in the Allen Ancient DNA Resource, 16,496 people, by where and when they lived. 68% come from Europe; the first farmers spread out of Anatolia at about a kilometre a year; and in Britain, none of 76 men before 2500 BCE carried the Y line R1b.
seo_description: A map of 16,496 ancient human genomes: sampling bias, the spread of farming and the Y chromosome turnover in Europe after 2500 BCE.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Ancient DNA on the map' in black, red and blue on pale paper, beside a map of Europe and the Near East covered in small dots coloured from dark brown for the oldest to blue for the most recent, densest in Britain, Denmark, Hungary and Austria. Text: 16,496 ancient genomes, placed where and when they lived.
